 Flour Recall: More Than 4,000 Bags Just Received the FDA’s Highest Risk Warning
 Nungning20/Getty Images 
 By 
 Alex Vance 
 Published on Oct. 29, 2026
 Getting your Trinity Audio player ready... 
 Testing revealed an unexpected ingredient in several products.
 For people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivities, checking food labels isn’t just a habit—it’s an important part of staying healthy. Additionally, an estimated one-third of Americans limit their gluten consumption “due to health concerns,” according to NYU Langone Health .
 For all these reasons, it’s easy to see why a nationwide recall of several gluten-free baking mixes is raising concerns after testing found something that shouldn’t have been there: undeclared wheat gluten.
 What happened?
 On September 18, GF Blends first announced it was recalling Truly AIP All Purpose Flour, Truly AIP Bread Mix, and EAT G.A.N.G.S.T.E.R. Flat Bread Pizza Mix because they may contain undeclared wheat gluten—and on October 28, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) classified the recall as Class I, its most serious risk level . This means there is “a reasonable probability” that the product will cause serious health consequences for consumers.
 Here’s why: The recalled products were reporetedly manufactured using plantain flour supplied by a food manufacturer with a gluten-free label and certification. But third-party testing revealed that the plantain flour contained gluten levels that “significantly” exceeded the FDA’s threshold of 20 parts per million for foods labeled gluten-free. The affected product mixes also tested above that threshold.
 This type of labeling issue can be especially concerning for people with celiac disease or a wheat gluten allergy. Stanford Medicine experts explain that when a person with celiac disease eats gluten, the immune system attacks and damages part of the small intestine, which can lead to symptoms such as weight loss, fatigue, abdominal pain, vomiting, or diarrhea. For those with wheat gluten allergies, consumption can cause eczema, hives, hay fever, or, in severe cases, anaphylactic shock .
 Which flour products are affected?
 The recalled flour mixes were sold nationwide to customers until September 12, 2026, on eatgangster.com, trulyaip.com, and Amazon.
 The FDA provides the following details:
  Gluten Free Truly AIP All Purpose Baking Mix Flour, 15.3 oz. (1495 bags) 
 Lot numbers and best-by dates:
 260225; 2/25/28
 260610; 6/10/28
 Gluten Free Truly AIP Rustic Bread Mix, 14 oz. (986 bags) 
 Lot numbers and best-by dates:
 260417; 4/17/28
 260617; 12/17/27
 Gluten Free EAT G.A.N.G.S.T.E.R Pizza Crust and Flatbread Mix, 5.8 oz. (2,163 bags) and 3.98 lbs. (20 bags) 
 Lot numbers and best-by dates:
 260327; 7/27/27 and 9/27/27
 260803; 2/03/28
 GF Blends says it “immediately” notified customers of the recall once confirmed, along with flagging all affected lots. Consumers with the recalled mixes are told to either throw them away or return them to the place of purchase for a full refund.
